patch.value: The published-artifact gate never executes pm-mcp: two of three declared bins resolve to the same file and the third — which already shipped dead once — has zero release coverage

Filed 2026-07-31 from a source read of the release pipeline plus an empirical check of the shipped build. Duplicate check performed across all statuses for pm-mcp, MCP server entrypoint, published verification, tarball smoke, and bin alias lineages: pm-qtbc is the closed defect this generalizes and is deliberately NOT re-opened or re-parented (it is a closed parentless item); pm-lpqln4 owns the bunx probe's inert-token defect and is a sibling of this one, not a parent; pm-ygli86 owns driving a released tarball through a scripted agent session; pm-rtn5h6 owns the escape ratchet as a policy. None of them asserts that dist/mcp/server.js executes from a published artifact. No existing item does.

The published-artifact verification executes the pm-mcp bin from the published package under both npx and bunx, not only the CLI bin; The pm-mcp assertion is a JSON-RPC handshake (initialize request answered with a well-formed result carrying the server name and protocol version), never an exit-code or --version check, because the pm-qtbc failure mode was a silent exit 0 with no output; The gate resolves the bin through a symlinked install path equivalent to a real npm global/npx install, since pm-qtbc only manifested under symlinked argv[1] and is invisible from an in-repo run; A deliberately broken main-module guard reintroducing the pm-qtbc defect makes the gate fail, asserted by a negative-control test rather than by review; Every entry in package.json bin is covered by at least one published-artifact assertion, and the mapping from bin name to distinct entrypoint file is checked so two aliases of one file are not counted as two covered surfaces; The bin-to-coverage mapping is derived from package.json at gate time, so adding a fourth bin without coverage fails the gate instead of silently shipping unverified

## Measured at HEAD (b7651d793), 2026-07-31

`package.json` declares three bins:

    pm-cli  -> dist/cli.js
    pm      -> dist/cli.js
    pm-mcp  -> dist/mcp/server.js

Two of the three are aliases of one file. `dist/mcp/server.js` is a genuinely distinct 27,625-byte entrypoint, and it is the surface every MCP-based agent actually runs.

### Coverage, counted

`grep -rn "pm-mcp" scripts/release/ .github/workflows/` returns **zero matches**.

Pre-publish (`scripts/smoke-npx-from-pack.mjs`) asserts: bare npx `--version` + `--help`, and the `pm-cli` alias `--version` + `--help`. Post-publish (`scripts/release/verify-published-release.mjs`) asserts three executor probes: `npx-direct`, `npx-package`, `bunx`. Every one of these six assertions terminates in `dist/cli.js`.

So the release pipeline verifies one entrypoint six times and the other zero times. The step is named "Verify published package on npm, npx, and bunx", which reads as runtime coverage rather than entrypoint coverage, and that is why the gap is invisible in review.

### Why this specific bin is the wrong one to leave uncovered

pm-qtbc is closed with resolution "Fixed pm-mcp main-module detection by realpath-resolving symlinked npm bin argv paths." That defect had two properties that matter here:

1. It was **invisible in-repo**. It manifested only under a symlinked `argv[1]`, i.e. only from a real npm/npx install. No in-repo test could have caught it.
2. It failed as a **silent exit 0 with no JSON-RPC output**. An exit-code probe passes. A `--version` probe passes.

Both properties survive today. A regression of pm-qtbc would ship green through every gate in the pipeline.

### The probe shape is also wrong where it exists

Verified empirically against the shipped build:

    $ node dist/cli.js ZZZ_NOT_A_COMMAND --version
    2026.7.31
    exit=0

`--version` short-circuits before subcommand resolution, so an arbitrary token in that position is silently ignored and exit stays 0. This is the mechanism behind pm-lpqln4 (the bunx probe passes `pm` in the argument position, where it is inert). It is recorded here because it also sets the requirement for this item: a `--version` assertion cannot distinguish a working entrypoint from a dead one, so the pm-mcp assertion must be a JSON-RPC `initialize` handshake, not an exit code.

### Relationship to the escape ratchet

pm-rtn5h6 requires every escaped defect to land a gate that would have caught it. pm-qtbc escaped to a published artifact, was fixed, and landed no gate — grep proves it. This item is the concrete instance that ratchet exists to prevent, and is useful as its first worked example rather than as a competing policy.
